name: UDA1334A I2S stereo DAC
description: NXP UDA1334ATS low-power stereo audio DAC with I2S input and a built-in PLL, so it needs no master clock: just BCLK, WSEL and DIN. Gives a line-level stereo output (about 0.9 V RMS full scale) for headphones or an amplifier, 16-100 kHz sample rates. Sold as: Adafruit I2S Stereo Decoder - UDA1334A Breakout (product 3678), 3-5 V supply with onboard 3.3 V regulator, 3.5 mm jack, 9-pin power/I2S/line-out header plus 6-pin control header.
eli5: Turns the digital sound your board sends out into a real audio signal you can plug headphones or a speaker amplifier into.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply in, 3-5 V; the onboard MIC5225 regulator makes 3.3 V for the DAC

pins.name: 3VO
pins.description: 3.3 V OUTPUT of the onboard regulator (up to about 100 mA spare), not a supply input: leave unconnected

pins.name: WSEL
pins.description: I2S word select / left-right clock (LRCLK); 3.3-5 V logic

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: I2S serial data in, both channels; 3.3-5 V logic

pins.name: BCLK
pins.description: I2S bit clock; 3.3-5 V logic (at most 64 x the word-select rate)

pins.name: Lout
pins.description: Left line-level output (about 0.9 V RMS full scale, AC-coupled), also on the 3.5 mm jack; to an amplifier input, not a GPIO

pins.name: AGND
pins.description: Clean analog ground: reference for Lout/Rout when wiring to an amplifier

pins.name: Rout
pins.description: Right line-level output, also on the 3.5 mm jack; to an amplifier input, not a GPIO

pins.name: SCLK
pins.description: System clock in (27 MHz, video mode only). In audio mode it selects the rate range: low (10k pull-down) = 16-50 kHz, high = 50-100 kHz

pins.name: SF1
pins.description: Serial format select 1 (10k pull-down). SF1/SF0 low/low = I2S (default)

pins.name: MUTE
pins.description: Soft mute: high mutes the output (10k pull-down = playing)

pins.name: SF0
pins.description: Serial format select 0 (10k pull-down); 3.3 V logic only, not 5 V tolerant

pins.name: PLL
pins.description: PLL mode (10k pull-down = audio mode); 3-level input, 3.3 V logic only, not 5 V tolerant

pins.name: DEEM
pins.description: De-emphasis on when high (44.1 kHz, audio mode; 10k pull-down = off). Clock output in video mode

supplierQuery: Adafruit UDA1334A I2S stereo decoder breakout 3678
buildNotes: Only VIN, GND, WSEL, DIN and BCLK are needed; every control pin has a 10k pull-down giving I2S format, audio mode, no mute, no de-emphasis.
No MCLK: the PLL locks to WSEL. With SCLK left low the sample rate must be 16-50 kHz (e.g. 22050 or 44100).
The output is line level (about 0.9 V RMS): fine for headphones or an amplifier input, too weak to drive a bare speaker.
PLL and SF0 are not 5 V tolerant: drive them only from 3.3 V logic or leave them unconnected.
Keep the audio ground (AGND) and the board ground on one point to avoid hum.

example.code:
from machine import I2S, Pin
import math, struct, time

RATE = 22050  # UDA1334A audio mode with SCLK low (board default): 16-50 kHz
audio = I2S(0, sck=Pin({BCLK}), ws=Pin({WSEL}), sd=Pin({DIN}), mode=I2S.TX,
            bits=16, format=I2S.STEREO, rate=RATE, ibuf=8000)

FREQ = 441
N = RATE // FREQ * 4            # whole cycles, so the buffer loops cleanly
buf = bytearray(N * 4)          # 16-bit left + 16-bit right per frame
for i in range(N):
    s = int(8000 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * FREQ * i / RATE))
    struct.pack_into('<hh', buf, i * 4, s, s)

time.sleep(1)
print('playing')
t = time.ticks_ms()
while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t) < 2000:
    audio.write(buf)
audio.deinit()
print('done')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Plays a 441 Hz tone for two seconds, then stops
